title: Instruction ghosting — notes & quick probes
content:
Short description:
This is a scratch note capturing repeated, small experiments where instructions from earlier examples or system messages seem to 'ghost' into later outputs even when the explicit instruction is removed. Goal is to codify reproduceable probes and quick mitigation hacks to test in Optimize pipelines.

Raw observations (high-level):
- Ghosting shows up worst when examples are semantically similar and contain a strong directive (e.g., "always add a justification").
- Removing the directive from later exemplars doesn't fully remove behaviour; model still sometimes appends justification-like text.
- Occurs across temperature settings but is amplified with higher temp; also visible at temp=0 in deterministic repetition cases.
- Appears in both chat-style prompts and single-shot templates with few-shot block.

Quick probes (examples to repro locally):
1) Few-shot list-to-one mapping: 3 exemplars that end with "(include justification)" then 2 new exemplars without it. See whether outputs on new items still include parentheses or justification sentences.
2) System message ghost: system says "You are concise and always give a one-line reason." Then a user message overwrites with "Only give the answer, no reason." Measure proportion of responses including reasons.

Concrete sample prompt (use in a test harness):
---PROMPT BLOCK---
System: You are a helpful assistant.
Ex1: Q: Why is the sky blue? A: Scattering of sunlight. (always include a one-line reason)
Ex2: Q: Why do leaves turn red? A: Pigment changes. (always include a one-line reason)
Ex3: Q: Why do stars twinkle? A: Atmospheric turbulence. (always include a one-line reason)

Now: Q: Why does metal expand when heated?
---END BLOCK---
Then run an alternate where the examples are identical but the parenthetical "(always include...)" removed from Ex3 and the test question is the same. Compare tokens after answer.

Observed failure modes (notes):
- Partial ghosting: assistant emits a short appended clause that looks like a justification fragment rather than full structured reasoning.
- Token-level bleed: phrase patterns such as "because of" or "this means" appear with higher probability near the answer boundary.
- Position matters: ghosting stronger when directive is at the end of example lines (suffix placement).

Hypotheses: 
- Model weights encode a positional association for strong suffix directives; few-shot exemplars at end-of-sequence shape the next-token distribution more than embedded directives.
- KV-cache or attention residuals keep the instruction pattern alive across the attention window, even when explicit text removed from later exemplars.
- The model learns a short-hand macro: if many exemplars contain a meta-tag, it creates an implicit template that survives small edits.

Quick mitigation ideas to test (prioritized):
1) Neutralizing suffix tokens: after the few-shot block, insert a short sentinel token sequence that explicitly nullifies prior meta-instructions (e.g., "<<END_EXAMPLES>>\nNote: ignore prior meta tags"). Measure regression.
2) Anchor re-assertion: explicitly restate the desired absence of the clue in system message (but this may cause adversarial layering).
3) Example diversity: rotate directive position (prefix/mid/suffix) or obfuscate directive via paraphrase to reduce positional bias.
4) Explicit negative exemplars: include 1-2 counterexamples showing the format without the directive.
5) Template-level compression: compile exemplars into condensed facts rather than full sentences (reduce repetition).

Planned experiments (short todo):
- [ ] Run sweep across temps {0, 0.2, 0.7, 1.0} with and without sentinel neutralizer. Measure ghosting rate (binary flag: contains justification-like phrase).
- [ ] Test on models: small, medium, and large family (open models we have in hosted sandbox). Log token-level deltas.
- [ ] Ablation: move directive location (end vs start).
- [ ] Add negative exemplars test and measure improvement.

Notes to self / heuristics that worked in quick runs:
- Inserting a short explicit instruction immediately before the test query like "Answer only the question, do not add reasons." reduces ghosting by ~40% in a tiny sample (n=50) but sometimes produces terse, under-informative answers. Tradeoff.
- When using anchors, interleaving a punctuation-heavy separator ("---") helps re-segment model attention but is brittle.

Unresolved questions:
- Is this primarily a prompting artifact or something that requires model re-training/fine-tuning?
- Does quantization amplify ghosting because of token-probability smoothing? (need to test on quantized dedicated nodes)
- Are there metricable signals in attention maps (if reachable) that show residual weight on directive tokens?

References / links (quick):
- Slack thread: ghosting-thread (linked above).
- Related GH PR: prompt-experiments/pull/78 (adds sentinel tests).

Next steps (practical):
- Spin up a small eval job in Optimize harness with 1k synthetic cases, compare baseline vs sentinel vs negative-exemplar strategies. Tag results and share with Diego for prioritization.
- If promising, draft a short internal note for product-hosted-api about recommended prompt sanitizers for customer docs.

Random musings (scratch):
- Could build an automated "de-ghostifier" that detects persistent directive tokens in few-shot sets and suggests counterexamples or sentinel insertion. Possibly integrated as a pre-send transformer.
- Might be worth a small user study: do humans expect the justification to persist? Is this sometimes desirable (consistency) vs a bug?

End of notes.
